headline: Looking for something to do this weekend? Here are the Top 5 local events for Nov. 13–15
subhead: The Stuart Air Show, Friday Motown in Vero Beach, PalmCon, a free Fort Pierce Beach Jam and Stuart's Hispanic Heritage Festival headline the weekend.
teaser: From Friday night's Stuart Air Show and Motown in Vero Beach to PalmCon, a Fort Pierce waterfront festival and Sunday's Hispanic Heritage Festival, here are five weekend picks.
body:
The Stuart Air Show returns to Witham Field this weekend, while a comic convention, a free Fort Pierce waterfront festival, live Motown music in Vero Beach and a Sunday cultural celebration offer plenty of other ways to get out around the Treasure Coast.

Here are five events worth considering from **Friday evening, Nov. 13, through Sunday, Nov. 15**, across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

## 1. Stuart Air Show, Stuart

**When:** Friday, Nov. 13, 4–10 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 14–15, 9 a.m.–5 p.m. **Where:** Witham Field, 1895 SE Flying Fortress Lane, Stuart. **Admission:** Tickets required; consult the organizer for current prices, discounts and parking arrangements.

The 37th annual Stuart Air Show brings three days of aviation displays and entertainment to Martin County Airport. Friday's evening program features twilight and nighttime flying, with fireworks and a drone-show finale planned. Saturday and Sunday offer daytime aerobatic performances, military and civilian aircraft, ground displays, food vendors and family activities.

The gates open at 4 p.m. Friday, with the show expected to begin around 5 p.m. Weekend gates open at 9 a.m., and opening ceremonies are scheduled for approximately 11:30 a.m. This is one of the region's largest outings of the weekend, so check parking instructions before leaving home. [Official Stuart Air Show information and tickets](https://www.stuartairshow.com/).

## 2. Mr Motwn at Riverside Theatre, Vero Beach

**When:** Friday, Nov. 13, 5:30–8:30 p.m. **Where:** Riverside Theatre, 3250 Riverside Park Drive, Vero Beach. **Admission:** Free for general outdoor seating; food, drinks and optional reserved cabanas cost extra.

Friday night in Indian River County brings the sounds of Motown to Riverside Theatre's outdoor Live in the Loop concert series. Mr Motwn is scheduled to perform an early-evening set, giving concertgoers a casual way to start the weekend.

The theatre's outdoor concert format lets visitors find an available nonreserved seat, bring a lawn chair or sit on the grass. Food and beverages are available for purchase on site. [Riverside Theatre's Loop music calendar](https://www.riversidetheatre.com/loop-music-calendar).

## 3. PalmCon: Treasure Coast, Port St. Lucie

**When:** Saturday, Nov. 14, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; Sunday, Nov. 15, 10 a.m.–5 p.m. **Where:** MIDFLORIDA Credit Union Event Center, 9221 SE Event Center Place, Port St. Lucie. **Admission:** Paid single-day and weekend passes; children ages 12 and younger enter free with a paid adult.

Comic books, costumes, collectibles and pop-culture fandom take over the event center for the two-day PalmCon convention. The event features artists, writers, vendors, cosplay participants and entertainment geared toward fans of comics and genre culture.

Visitors can choose a single-day ticket or make a weekend of it. The organizer lists advance and at-the-door ticket options, so buying ahead may offer better pricing. [PalmCon event details and tickets](https://palmcon.net/treasure-coast).

## 4. Pick, Paddle & Play Beach Jam, Fort Pierce

**When:** Saturday, Nov. 14, 10 a.m.–8 p.m. **Where:** Causeway Cove Marina, 601 Seaway Drive, Fort Pierce. **Admission:** Free.

The second annual Pick, Paddle & Play Beach Jam fills the Fort Pierce waterfront with live music, paddling and beach activities, food trucks, vendors, games and activities for families. The event also features a Community Resource Village connecting residents with local nonprofit and health organizations.

Organized by Stabilize Revitalize Fort Pierce, the festival raises awareness and support for local cancer-related causes, including Friends in Pink and CareBag. With admission free and activities scheduled throughout the day, visitors can stop by for a few hours or stay into the evening. [Beach Jam details](https://www.stabilizerevitalizefortpierce.org/pick-paddle-and-play-beach-jam).

## 5. Hispanic Heritage Festival, Stuart

**When:** Sunday, Nov. 15, 3–8 p.m. **Where:** Memorial Park Amphitheater, 300 SE Ocean Blvd., Stuart. **Admission:** Not specified in the city's calendar listing.

Sunday afternoon offers a community celebration of Hispanic heritage at Memorial Park Amphitheater. The City of Stuart lists the five-hour festival as a public calendar event, making it a possible afternoon or evening stop for residents who want to spend time in the heart of Stuart.

The city's listing does not yet provide a detailed entertainment schedule, vendor lineup or admission information, so check with the organizers before making plans. The event contact number is 772-626-4297. [City of Stuart festival listing](https://www.stuartfl.gov/m/calendar/event/detail/6883).

Event times, ticket availability and outdoor plans may change, especially following the recent heavy rains. Check the linked organizer pages for the latest updates before heading out. For more things to do throughout Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, browse the [Treasure Coast Today events calendar](https://treasurecoast.today/events.html).
